hero.title: Explore the universe. Discover what changes.
hero.lead: An interactive scientific platform to explore real SPHEREx observations and investigate the dynamic universe.
hero.disclaimer: Planet and orbits are an illustration. Every number on this page is either sourced or labelled as simulated.

explore.title: Every region of the sky tells a story.
explore.body: Point at any patch of sky by its coordinates — right ascension and declination — and The Origin Project asks the SPHEREx archive what it saw there, and when.

grid.detail: The coordinate system astronomers use to address any point on the sky.

constellations.detail: Landmarks for orientation: Orion, Ursa Major, Cassiopeia and Crux.

markers.detail: The five challenge targets, placed at their catalogue positions.

mission.title: The power of SPHEREx
mission.body: NASA's SPHEREx observatory photographs the whole sky again and again. Each repeat shows what moved or changed.
mission.disclaimer: The strips on the sphere are illustrative.

bands.note: Ranges per detector array, as published by NASA/IPAC IRSA. Bar heights are decorative.

a6.f2: Cold brown dwarfs glow brightest here

epochs.title: The universe changes.
epochs.body: Move through the epochs. Switch on the difference.

barnard.summary: A red dwarf 6 light-years away, the star with the largest known proper motion.
barnard.note: Expected shift across the span: up to 1.9 SPHEREx pixels.

epsindi.summary: Two brown dwarfs orbiting each other near Epsilon Indi A.

wise0855.summary: The coldest known brown dwarf; very faint in the near infrared.

rwaur.summary: A young star wrapped in dust, with irregular brightness changes.

rdra.summary: A pulsating red giant whose brightness rises and falls over months.
